Read-through with SLOOS overlay:
- Policy stance: Holding the funds rate at 4-1/4 to 4-1/2 percent with IORB at 4.4 percent keeps conditions restrictive. Slowing QT by cutting the Treasury redemption cap from $25B to $5B is a modestly dovish tilt on balance sheet policy; MBS cap stays at $35B. Waller’s dissent (favoring the faster runoff) limits how dovish this can be read.
- SLOOS signal: Banks continue to report tight credit for many borrowers. Standards remain tight in C&I and especially CRE, with banks citing economic outlook, industry-specific issues, and reduced risk tolerance. Consumer credit remains guarded, with higher minimum credit score requirements and banks expecting higher delinquencies and charge-offs. Demand appears mixed at best, with corporate and CRE loan demand still soft. Overall, SLOOS implies credit headwinds persist even as macro data show solid growth.
- Implication: The slower QT would normally be mildly supportive for risk assets and liquidity, but SLOOS’s persistence of tight standards, weak business loan demand, and expected deterioration in credit quality temper the read. Add the statement’s heightened uncertainty and the FSR’s elevated (though manageable) vulnerabilities, and the net sentiment remains positive but more cautious than a pure policy read.

Adjusted take: Mildly positive, moderated by ongoing tight bank credit conditions and credit-quality concerns from SLOOS.
